Controls say what they do again. Every button carries its words, and a new Labels setting decides how much of a control you see. Alongside that: a ready-to-save Unraid template for the append-only off-site server, a CPU cap for backups, and sixteen more languages.

## ✨ Added

- **Labels: decide how much of a control you see.** Settings, General, Labels. Four modes: the words, the symbol, both, or Reactive, which shows the symbol alone and slides the words back in when you point at it ([#178](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/bombvault/issues/178), [#184](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/bombvault/issues/184)). Icon-only buttons had replaced text across the app, and two reports said the same thing from different angles: the icons were harder to read than words, and the mix of icon buttons and text buttons on one screen was inconsistent. Both are the same question, so both are answered by the same setting rather than by patching one screen at a time. Every button, badge and selector in the app now goes through one component that reads this mode, which is what makes the answer consistent instead of per screen. Buttons keep the same width in all four modes, so switching never reshuffles the page.
- **An Unraid container template for the append-only off-site server.** Settings, Off-site, guided setup, the **Unraid template (XML)** tab beside the docker run and compose recipes. Save it on the storage box under `/boot/config/plugins/dockerMan/templates-user/`, then Docker, Add Container, and pick rest-server from the template dropdown. Reported from the support forum: the scripted deployment could not be edited in the Docker UI, so the reporter fell back to a Community Applications container and lost the append-only flags the recipe had set. The docker run recipe was never broken, verified end to end against a real rest-server. The problem is that a container Unraid did not create from a template has no template behind it, so the Docker tab offers no Edit form and the port, the path and the options can only be changed by deleting the container and retyping the whole command. The template keeps `--append-only --private-repos --htpasswd-file` in an editable OPTIONS field, so the immutability guarantee survives being adjusted later. The htpasswd line and the one-time password appear in the file's comments only, never in a template field, because Unraid keeps templates on the flash drive indefinitely.
- **A CPU cap for backups.** Settings, Paths & Storage, Backup CPU, visible in Advanced mode ([#189](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/bombvault/issues/189)). Reported as eight restic workers holding every core of a 12-thread laptop between 93% and 99% at 100 °C for the length of a backup. restic is a Go program, so with nothing set it takes every core the host has for compression and encryption, and the only throttles this engine had were for bandwidth. Zero still means every core, which is restic's own default, so an installation that never touches the field behaves exactly as before.
- **Animations: a manual dial.** Settings, General, Animations, with off, subtle and full. It sits alongside your system's reduced-motion setting and never overrides it, so turning motion down in the operating system still wins.
- **Recovery detects the repository's encryption mode instead of asking you.** Step 3 shows what it found at the top, rather than making you answer a question about a repository you are trying to recover precisely because you no longer have the instance that created it.
- **The drill, tamper and digest schedules accept an everyN cadence.** They also record their last run, so "every 3 days" now means every third day for those passes too rather than every night with a gate that usually closes.
- **A worked two-box off-site example in the documentation.** One complete setup with real values, five numbered steps, and a table saying what protected, NOT protected and inconclusive each mean. It calls out the two things that cost the reporter an evening: the receiver location is a path inside the container written relative to the host mount, and the Sending APP_KEY belongs to the sending box, not the receiving one.

## 🎨 Design

- **Every glyph in the app comes from one set.** Streamline's free Core Solid set, chosen per meaning rather than drawn one at a time, so the same idea looks the same everywhere it appears.
- **The folder browser is a dialog, at all nineteen places that open one.** It used to be an inline panel in some places and a dialog in others, which meant the same task looked like two different tasks depending on where you started it.
- **Number fields have their own steppers.** The browser's native ones differ per browser and per platform, and they were the last control in the app that did not follow its own sizing.
- **The off-site tab is one card per domain**, and notification channels have real on/off toggles instead of a channel that is configured but silently inactive.
- **The nav rail centres itself in glyph mode** instead of leaving the symbols hard against the left edge, and a control that hides its text explains itself in a real tooltip rather than a title attribute.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **Live backup progress disappeared about a minute in, and came back on a reload** ([#188](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/bombvault/issues/188)). Reported against a folder backup sitting at 18%. restic streams progress while it has something to report; scanning a large folder tree it goes quiet for minutes, and the dashboard treated that silence as proof the run had ended. Silence alone no longer ends a live line: the runs list is polled every ten seconds and each run carries its own status, so a quiet but living run keeps its line while a genuinely finished one still loses it.
- **The dashboard answered "what backs up next?" twice, by two mechanisms, and they could disagree** ([#187](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/bombvault/issues/187)). The summary tile ranked schedule text on an approximate period in the browser, while the activity log below it read the scheduler's real fire times. The approximation ranked a weekly Sunday cadence as seven days out whatever day it was, and could not walk an everyN schedule through its due gate. Two earlier faults came out of that. The tile now reads the same source as everything else.
- **The receiver refused a location that was written the way the field looks like it wants.** A path under `/mnt` is an absolute host path, and BombVault runs in a container where the host's `/mnt` is mounted elsewhere, so that path does not exist inside it. The error now names the relative path to use instead of only refusing.
- **The append-only tamper test could report a pass it had not proven.** A far side answering 404 was being read as a refusal; it is neither a refusal nor an acceptance. It reads inconclusive now, which records nothing and raises no alert, rather than claiming a protection that was never demonstrated.

## ⚡ Improved

- **A deletable off-site copy now reads as a gap on the protection card.** An off-site repository that is not marked append-only rendered as a grey dash saying "append-only not enabled", which on a card about ransomware reads as "does not apply". It applies: that copy can be deleted by whatever reaches the credentials on this machine. The row is amber now. The overall status chip deliberately does not move, because plenty of destinations cannot do append-only at all and a chip stuck on "needs attention" over a deliberate choice stops being a health signal.
- **The first page load is a fraction of its former size.** Translations load as separate chunks for the language in use instead of every language travelling with the first byte of the app.
- **Backups are logged and shown as one thing when they are one thing.** A run that produces several snapshots is correlated by a shared tag rather than assumed to produce exactly one.

## 🌐 Translations

- **Sixteen new languages, bringing BombVault to 42.** Every string in the app, not a subset with an English fallback.
- **Three documentation sections existed only in English and are now translated into all 25 languages.** Backup source detection, Generic Docker host, and Remote primary repositories. The gap was invisible in the navigation, because every page still built and read as complete. It was not invisible to a reader: the environment-variable table on every translated configuration page linked to an anchor that existed in English only, so that link went nowhere in 25 languages.
- **The worked off-site example is translated too**, so the one page that walks through a two-box setup end to end is not English-only.
